info.name: Task Processing Utility
info.summary: Auto-scales Task Processing workers based on the queue
info.description:
**Disclaimer: this project has been vibe coded.**
This application changes the number of Nextcloud Task Processing workers automatically. It calculates the number of workers from the number of tasks in the queue. The number of workers stays under a maximum value. The administrator sets this value.
The application gives workers to all the task types. Thus a large number of tasks of one type does not prevent the operation of the other types.
The Nextcloud administrator manual gives this method in "Improve AI task pickup speed". This application uses the same method. But it calculates the number of workers from the queue. It does not use a constant number of workers.
A supervisor service does the work. The supervisor is one static binary, written in Go. It reads the task queue and its configuration directly from the Nextcloud database. Then it starts workers with the command `occ taskprocessing-util:run`. Each worker operates on one task type only. Each worker stops after a time limit, and the supervisor starts a new one. Thus the workers get the new configuration.
## Setup
The application has two parts: this application, and a supervisor service that you must start yourself. **The application does nothing until the service operates.**
1. Enable the application: `occ app:enable task_proc_util` 2. Write a systemd unit that starts `apps/task_proc_util/bin/task_proc_util-supervisor` and gives it the path to your `config.php`. The service must operate on the same computer as Nextcloud. It must also operate as the user that owns `config.php`, usually `www-data`, because `occ` does not operate as a different user. An application password is not necessary. HTTP credentials are not necessary. Set `TimeoutStopSec=3600`, so the workers can complete the current task when the service stops. 3. Start the service, then examine its log. If `occ` does not operate, the supervisor shows the cause and stops immediately. 4. Adjust the settings in **Administration → Artificial Intelligence**: the main switch, the maximum number of workers, the poll interval, and the config reload interval.
The README file gives the complete systemd unit, the requirements, and all the flags and environment variables: https://github.com/kyteinsky/task_proc_util#setup
